name: Alibaba Cloud PolarDB
license: Proprietary managed service; open-source PolarDB for PostgreSQL (Apache 2.0) and PolarDB-X (Apache 2.0, storage engine GPL 2.0)
summary: Alibaba Cloud’s cloud-native relational databases: MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible clusters whose compute nodes share one copy of the data on distributed storage, plus PolarDB-X, a distributed MySQL-compatible edition.
intro: A PolarDB cluster separates compute from storage. One primary node takes writes and up to 15 read-only nodes take reads, and none of them keeps its own copy of the data: data files and redo logs live on a shared, distributed storage layer (PolarStore) that keeps several replicas in step with Parallel-Raft, reached over RDMA. Adding a reader therefore adds only compute, with no data to copy. If the primary fails, a reader takes over in under 10 seconds with no data loss. A proxy in front (PolarProxy) splits reads from writes, pools connections and offers read consistency levels. PolarDB for MySQL runs engine versions 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0; the Multi-master Cluster (Limitless) Edition lets every node write, an in-memory column index (IMCI) serves analytics on the same data, serverless clusters scale in PolarDB Capacity Units (about 1 core and 2 GB of memory each), and the Global Database Network replicates across regions with under 2 seconds of lag. Storage grows automatically, to 500 TB per cluster by default.

PolarDB for PostgreSQL has the same shape and is compatible with PostgreSQL 11, 14, 15, 16 and 17. It replicates to its readers from redo logs, so even a long DDL doesn’t make them lag, a write on the primary is immediately visible to all readers, and the cluster endpoint uses each node’s log sequence number (LSN) so a read never lands on a node that hasn’t caught up. A sibling edition, PolarDB for PostgreSQL (Compatible with Oracle), accepts Oracle stored procedures, data types and built-in functions, and a distributed form splits data across compute and data nodes. PolarDB for Xscale, or PolarDB-X, is different: a shared-nothing, MySQL-compatible database whose stateless compute nodes route queries and coordinate two-phase commits, while data nodes replicate with Paxos and a metadata service hands out global timestamps (TSO) for distributed MVCC. It shards on the primary key by default, adds clustered columnar indexes for analytics, and can start as a single-node Standard Edition and be upgraded in place to the distributed Enterprise Edition.

The managed services run on Alibaba Cloud, with Apsara Stack and DBStack for private deployments. Two parts are open source on GitHub: PolarDB for PostgreSQL under Apache 2.0, with stable branches built on PostgreSQL 11, 15 and 17 (17.11.1.0 in August 2026), and PolarDB-X, whose compute layer is Apache 2.0 and whose MySQL 8.0-based storage engine is GPL 2.0, with a Kubernetes operator. In US (Virginia) a serverless PCU costs $0.0794 an hour on Enterprise Edition and $0.07 on Standard Edition. PSL4 storage outside mainland China costs $0.000542 per GB-hour pay-as-you-go (about $0.40 per GB-month) or $0.2569 per GB-month on subscription, with storage replicated across two zones; single-zone storage costs half as much.
strengths: Read capacity without copies: up to 15 readers share one copy of the data, adding one takes minutes and costs only compute, and LSN-based consistency keeps reads from going stale
Existing drivers and tools work: MySQL 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0, PostgreSQL 11 to 17, an Oracle-compatible edition, and MySQL-compatible PolarDB-X
Failover in under 10 seconds with no data loss, and backups of terabytes in minutes from storage snapshots, without locking tables
Several ways to grow past one primary: serverless scaling, multi-writer Limitless clusters, PolarDB-X sharding, and column indexes for analytics on live data
The PostgreSQL edition and PolarDB-X are open source, so you can try them in Docker or run them on Kubernetes outside Alibaba Cloud
limits: The managed service is Alibaba Cloud’s (or its Apsara Stack and DBStack private clouds), and PolarDB for MySQL has no open-source release in the `polardb` GitHub organization, which carries only the PostgreSQL edition and PolarDB-X
PolarDB for MySQL offers engine versions 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0 (docs updated June 2026), while MySQL’s current long-term support series are 8.4 and 9.7

A Cluster Edition has one writer; scaling writes means the Limitless Edition or PolarDB-X, whose distributed Enterprise Edition is “highly compatible” with MySQL rather than fully compatible like its Standard Edition

Many price dimensions: edition, compute specification or serverless PCUs, storage class (ESSD PL0 to PL3, AutoPL, PSL4, PSL5), zone layout and region, and pay-as-you-go PSL4 storage costs about 1.5 times the subscription rate
Headline figures such as up to 6 times the transaction throughput and 400 times the analytical performance of open-source databases are Alibaba’s own

snippet.title: A primary and a read-only node sharing one data directory, in the open-source PolarDB for PostgreSQL 17 image (run on PolarDB 17.11.1.0)
source: # the primary listens on 5432, a read-only node on 5433
psql -p 5432 -c "CREATE TABLE orders (id int PRIMARY KEY, total numeric);" \
-c "INSERT INTO orders SELECT g, g * 1.5 FROM generate_series(1, 100000) g;"
psql -p 5433 -c "SELECT pg_is_in_recovery(), count(*), sum(total) FROM orders;"
# ERROR:  cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction
du -sh /var/polardb/*     # each node keeps only local state; the data is shared

items.name: PolarDB for MySQL, Cluster Edition
items.text: One primary and up to 15 read-only nodes on shared PolarStore storage, with failover in under 10 seconds.

items.name: PolarDB for MySQL, Multi-master Cluster (Limitless)
items.text: Every node accepts reads and writes; Alibaba says write throughput grows linearly with nodes, and switchover takes 5 to 10 seconds.

items.name: PolarDB for MySQL, Standard Edition
items.text: The same kernel on ordinary ECS instances, with ESSD cloud disks or PolarStore underneath, on x86 or Arm (Yitian 710).

items.name: PolarDB for PostgreSQL
items.text: Shared-storage clusters like the MySQL edition, plus a distributed form with compute and data nodes for manual sharding below 1 PB.

items.name: PolarDB for PostgreSQL (Compatible with Oracle)
items.text: Accepts Oracle stored procedures, data types, SQL and built-in functions with minimal changes.

items.name: PolarDB for Xscale (PolarDB-X)
items.text: Shared-nothing, MySQL-compatible, Paxos replication and TSO transactions; a Standard Edition upgrades in place to a distributed Enterprise Edition.

sections.title: Serverless compute list prices
sections.intro: PolarDB for MySQL serverless clusters, billed per PCU-second and settled hourly. Checked 11 October 2026 (page updated July 2026).
notes: 1 PCU is about 1 core and 2 GB of memory; serverless clusters scale in steps of 0.5 PCU.

Storage is billed separately. PSL4 with a hot-standby storage cluster in a second zone: $0.000542 per GB-hour pay-as-you-go or $0.2569 per GB-month on subscription in Hong Kong and international regions, $0.000486 per GB-hour or $0.2308 per GB-month in the Chinese mainland. Single-zone storage costs half as much.

story: Before PolarDB, high-performance cloud databases usually ran on an instance store: a VM with a local SSD. Alibaba’s engineers listed the problems. Capacity was limited, the database had to replicate itself to survive a disk failure, the general-purpose file system’s kernel overhead wasted the speed of RDMA and NVMe, and there was no way for several database nodes to share one copy of the data. Open-source distributed file systems such as HDFS and Ceph had much higher latency than local disks.

Wei Cao and colleagues at Alibaba built PolarFS, a distributed file system with its network and I/O stacks in user space, and on top of it POLARDB, modified from AliSQL, Alibaba’s fork of MySQL and InnoDB. The primary and the read-only nodes share redo log and data files in the same directory on PolarFS. They described it at VLDB 2018, when it had recently become available on Alibaba Cloud, and Alibaba Cloud released PolarDB outside China in July 2019.

The family then widened: PostgreSQL and Oracle-compatible editions, and PolarDB-X, which started as a way past the scaling limits of the core transaction system behind Tmall’s Double Eleven sales. Alibaba open-sourced PolarDB for PostgreSQL under Apache 2.0 in 2021 and PolarDB-X that November. Research kept going: PolarDB Serverless (SIGMOD 2021) pulled memory into a remote pool and recovered from failures 5.3 times faster, PolarDB-IMCI (SIGMOD 2023) added a column index that sped up TPC-H queries by up to 149 times with under 5% impact on transactions, and multi-primary and CXL memory-pool designs won SIGMOD’s best industrial paper awards in 2024 and 2025.

choices.choice: Shared storage instead of a full copy per replica
choices.why: Instance stores capped capacity and couldn’t survive a disk failure without the database replicating itself. With one copy on a storage cluster, compute and storage scale separately, compute nodes hold no persistent state, and readers can be added without copying data.

choices.choice: A user-space I/O path on RDMA and NVMe
choices.why: Research the team cited found about 20,000 instructions executed to complete a single 4 KB I/O through the legacy kernel stack. PolarFS is compiled into the database process and bypasses the kernel, which brought its write latency close to a local file system on SSD.

Raft’s strict ordering held back I/O on hardware with latencies of tens of microseconds. Databases tolerate I/O completing out of order, so ParallelRaft acknowledges, commits and applies log entries out of order while keeping replicas consistent.

choices.choice: Start from MySQL rather than a new engine
choices.why: Modifying AliSQL, Alibaba’s existing MySQL fork, meant the new service kept MySQL’s protocol and SQL. Alibaba still sells PolarDB on moving MySQL 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0 databases without code changes.
